text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former managing director at Zimbabwe Newspapers Simba Makoni this week said political interference and discomfort over lack of transparency and accountability in the operations of the organisation led to his suspension and dismissal.

- The Zimbabwe Catholic Bishops Conference has been split over publication of its report on the atrocities committed in the Matebeleland region by the Fifth Brigade wing of the national army in the 1980s.
- The cash-strapped government used an estimated Z$200 million from treasury to host the just-ended 33rd Organisation of African Unity heads of state and government summit.

- The World Conservation Union says it will support the Zimbabwe government's proposal to have the African elephant downlisted and allow for international trade in ivory at the forthcoming Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species.
- A Zimbabwean farmer lost 20 head of cattle valued at more than Z$140,000 from suspected poisoning after he fed them stockfeed from a reputable local company.
